q-10884.name: Question 1
q-10884.worked_solution:
Computing the first derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{5}+4{x}^{3}-10{x}^{2}) \\  & =5\cdot 3{x}^{4}+3\cdot 4{x}^{2}-2\cdot 10x \\  & =15{x}^{4}+12{x}^{2}-20x\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(15{x}^{4}+12{x}^{2}-20x) \\  & =15\cdot 4{x}^{3}+2\cdot 12x-20 \\  & =60{x}^{3}+24x-20.\end{aligned}
$$

q-10884.html:
Question 1
?

Calculate d2ydx2 for y=3x5+4x3−10x2.

a
30x3+24x−20
b
60x3+24x−22
c
60x3+48x−20
d
60x3−24x−20
e
60x3+24x−20
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Computing the first derivative, we get dydx=ddx(3x5+4x3−10x2)=5⋅3x4+3⋅4x2−2⋅10x=15x4+12x2−20x.

Computing the second derivative, we get d2ydx2=ddx(15x4+12x2−20x)=15⋅4x3+2⋅12x−20=60x3+24x−20.

q-342862.name: Question 2
q-342862.worked_solution:
Computing the first derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{3}-8x) \\  & =3\cdot 3{x}^{2}-8 \\  & =9{x}^{2}-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(9{x}^{2}-8) \\  & =2\cdot 9x \\  & =18x.\end{aligned}
$$

q-342868.name: Question 3
q-342868.worked_solution:
Computing the first derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{x}^{8}}{4}+x-\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{x}^{8}}{4}+x-4{x}^{-1/2}) \\  & =8\cdot \frac{{x}^{7}}{4}+1-(-\frac{1}{2})\cdot 4{x}^{-3/2} \\  & =2{x}^{7}+1+2{x}^{-3/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{7}+1+2{x}^{-3/2}) \\  & =7\cdot 2{x}^{6}+0+(-\frac{3}{2})\cdot 2{x}^{-5/2} \\  & =14{x}^{6}-3{x}^{-5/2} \\  & =14{x}^{6}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{{x}^{5}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

fields.input_html: 14x6−3x5/2​

q-343086.name: Question 4
q-343086.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can rewrite the function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{{x}^{5}-{x}^{2}+x}{4{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}}{4}-\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{4x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the first derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{x}^{3}}{4}-\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{4x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{x}^{3}}{4}-\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{4}{x}^{-1}) \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}}{4}-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{3{x}^{2}}{4}-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{-2}) \\  & =\frac{3x}{2}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, computing the third derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{‴}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{3x}{2}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{-3}) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}-\frac{3}{2}{x}^{-4} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}-\frac{3}{2{x}^{4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that we can rewrite the function as follows:

f(x)=x5−x2+x4x2=x34−14+14x

Now, computing the first derivative, we get f′(x)=ddx(x34−14+14x)=ddx(x34−14+14x−1)=3x24−14x−2.

Computing the second derivative, we get f″(x)=ddx(3x24−14x−2)=3x2+12x−3.

Finally, computing the third derivative, we get f‴(x)=ddx(3x2+12x−3)=32−32x−4=32−32x4.
